author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 겨울철새 수천 마리 · 나그네새 수천 마리 · 텃새 수백 마리
habitat: 농경지·개활지, 하천가 절벽, 숲 가장자리, 도시

months.note: 1년 내내 볼 수 있다. 영남 도시 지역 조사에서 번식기는 3월 전반부터 8월 전반까지로 추정되었고, 어린새가 둥지를 떠나는 시기는 5월 후반~6월에 몰린다.

summary: 들판과 도시 하늘에서 비교적 흔히 만나는 작은 매류로, 천연기념물이다. 바람을 안고 한자리에 떠서 날개를 빠르게 치는 정지비행으로 땅 위를 살피다가 들쥐나 작은 새를 덮친다. 절벽 틈이나 버려진 까치둥지뿐 아니라 고층 건물과 아파트의 틈에도 둥지를 튼다.

points.en: broad black band near tail tip

sexes.male: 머리와 꼬리가 청회색이고, 꼬리 끝에 굵은 검은 띠와 가는 흰 테가 있다. 적갈색 등의 검은 반점이 암컷보다 적다.
sexes.female: 머리부터 꼬리까지 윗면이 적갈색이고 검은 반점과 가로무늬가 촘촘하다. 갈색 꼬리에 검은 가로띠가 여러 줄 있으며, 몸이 수컷보다 크다.

young: 암컷 성조와 닮았으나 아랫면의 세로줄이 더 굵고, 납막·눈테·다리의 노란색이 더 옅다.

similar.how: 날개가 더 길고 뾰족하며 꼬리는 더 짧다. 등이 적갈색이 아니라 어두운 청회색이고, 허벅지와 아래꼬리덮깃이 적갈색이다.
훨씬 무겁고 다부진 몸에 검은 머리와 굵은 뺨선을 가졌다. 등은 청회색으로 적갈색이 없고, 아랫면에 가로줄 무늬가 촘촘하다.

art.subject: Common Kestrel (Falco tinnunculus), adult male, as seen over Korean farmland in early spring: head and nape blue-grey, finely streaked darker on the crown, with a narrow black moustachial stripe dropping below the eye and pale buff cheeks and throat; back, scapulars and upperwing coverts warm rufous-chestnut with small black triangular spots; primaries blackish. Rump and tail blue-grey, the tail unbarred except for a broad black subterminal band and a narrow white tip. Underparts warm buff, spotted and streaked blackish on the breast and flanks. Underwing whitish, finely spotted, with darker tips. Eye dark brown with a yellow eye-ring; cere yellow; bill short, hooked, bluish-grey with a dark tip; legs and feet yellow with black claws.
art.pose: hovering in mid-air facing into the wind, wings beating fast, tail fanned and angled down, head held perfectly still looking at the ground
art.scene: Korean farmland in early spring: harvested rice paddies with pale stubble, an earthen levee path, dry reeds along an irrigation ditch, low wooded hills in the distance under a clear pale-blue sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, in flight seen from above: blue-grey head and tail, broad black subterminal tail band with white tip, rufous back and inner wing spotted black, contrasting blackish outer wing

adult male, in flight seen from below: blue-grey head with narrow black moustache and pale throat, buff body finely streaked and spotted dark, pale finely spotted underwing with darker tips, long tail showing the black subterminal band

adult female, hovering, seen from below and slightly to the side with the tail fanned: rufous-brown head with narrow dark moustache, rufous-brown back and wings densely barred and spotted dark, brown tail with many narrow dark bars and a broad black subterminal band
art.build: Small, slim falcon, 33cm (male) to 38cm (female), about the length of a Feral Pigeon but slimmer and longer-tailed. Rounded head, large dark eye. Wings long and pointed, but broader and blunter-tipped than a Hobby's; at rest the wingtips fall well short of the tail tip, leaving much of the tail exposed. Tail long, slightly rounded at the tip. Habitually hovers on fast-beating wings with the tail fanned and the head held perfectly still, then drops onto voles; also watches from bare branches and earth banks.
avoid: Do not paint a dark slate-grey back; that is Eurasian Hobby or Peregrine. The kestrel's back is rufous.
Do not paint rufous thighs and vent (Hobby), or a broad black hood and thick moustache (Peregrine).
Do not bar the adult male's tail; it is plain blue-grey apart from the black band and white tip.
Do not paint a short tail, or wingtips reaching the tail tip at rest.
Do not paint a yellow or orange iris; the eye is dark brown.
